Stapel.et: From Middle Low German stāpel, from Old Saxon stapol, from Proto-West Germanic *stapul (“pillar, post, basis, foundation”). Doublet of Etappe and Staffel.

s: forklift, forklift truck, lift truck, jitney, fork truck (a small industrial vehicle with a power-operated fork-like pronged platform that can be raised and lowered for insertion under a load, often on pallets, to be lifted and moved)
by the pile, in batch, in stacks, stacks of, batches of, piles of
to trudge, to walk heavily (e.g. through snow)

Stapfe.et: Middle High German stapfe, Old High German stapho.

s: Stapelfeld (a municipality of Stormarn district, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany)
Stapelfeld.et: By surface analysis, Stapel (“stack, batch”) + Feld (“field”). Cognate with English Staplefield.
